a) a cluster design is the best choice to minimize the stop‐band width, and b) the stop‐band is cancelled in a symmetric design.
the lattice design of the SSC has been optimized to the best possible degree and that there is no significant room for further improvement.
the cluster design is the best design for large hadrons and that the antisymmetric design is the best choice.

the following aspects of lattice design: (a) the design of the lattice, (b) the IR design, (c) the design of beam‐beam interaction and the beam‐beam limit, and (d) the design of optics and beam dynamics for the collider.
the design of the lattice, the beam dynamics and the beam‐optical parameters, and the beam‐dynamics limitations of the lattice.
the following: (1) the design and analysis of the lattice of the SSC and (2) the design and development of new lattice concepts for the SSC and future colliders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design of a lattice is an iterative process.
the lattice design for the SSC has been well thought out and is very good.
there is no single best lattice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cluster design of the SSC lattice has been optimized.
the cluster design is a very good design for a high energy hadron collider.

the lattice design is a compromise of the following: (1) the beam optics, (2) the beam dynamics, (3) the beam‐beam interaction, (4) the beam stability, (5) the lattice cost, (6) the lattice cost‐effectiveness, and (7) the lattice reliability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lattice design should be done by considering the physics of beam dynamics.
a symmetric design is more efficient in terms of cost and performance.
the IR design is a critical part of the collider lattice design and that it can have a significant impact on the overall performance of the collider.
